statement: For a value v occurring in root, let node(v) be the unique node with value v. For values a,b occurring in root, let d(a,b) be the number of edges on the unique simple path between node(a) and node(b) in the underlying undirected tree. A leaf value is a value l such that node(l) has no children, i.e. Node(l, Null, Null) occurs in root. The function returns a result r, r is a leaf value of root, and for every leaf value l of root, d(k,l) >= d(k,r).
preconditions: root is a finite nonempty binary tree (root != Null); every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000; all node values are distinct; the number of nodes is between 1 and 1000; and there is a node in root whose value equals k (hence k is one of the node values).

statement: The function returns a result r; in particular it does not fail, panic, overflow, or go out of bounds.
preconditions: root is a finite nonempty binary tree (root != Null); every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000; all node values are distinct; the number of nodes is between 1 and 1000; and there is a node in root whose value equals k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, the node Node(r, Null, Null) occurs in root; equivalently, r is the value of a leaf node of root.
preconditions: root is a finite nonempty binary tree (root != Null); every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000; all node values are distinct; the number of nodes is between 1 and 1000; and there is a node in root whose value equals k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every leaf value l of root, d(k,l) >= d(k,r), where d(a,b) is the number of edges on the unique simple path between the unique nodes with values a and b.
preconditions: root is a finite nonempty binary tree (root != Null); every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000; all node values are distinct; the number of nodes is between 1 and 1000; and there is a node in root whose value equals k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if the node with value k is a leaf of root, then r = k.
preconditions: root is a finite nonempty binary tree (root != Null); every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000; all node values are distinct; the number of nodes is between 1 and 1000; and there is a node in root whose value equals k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if the node with value k has at least one child that is a leaf, then the node with value r is a leaf child of the node with value k; equivalently, d(k,r) = 1 and r is a leaf value.
preconditions: root is a finite nonempty binary tree (root != Null); every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000; all node values are distinct; the number of nodes is between 1 and 1000; and there is a node in root whose value equals k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if the root node itself has value k, then r is a leaf value and for every leaf value l of root, depth(l) >= depth(r), where depth(x) is the number of edges from the root to the node with value x.
preconditions: root is a finite nonempty binary tree (root != Null); every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000; all node values are distinct; the number of nodes is between 1 and 1000; and there is a node in root whose value equals k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if N is the number of nodes of root, then d(k,r) <= N - 1, where d(a,b) is the number of edges on the unique simple path between the unique nodes with values a and b.
preconditions: root is a finite nonempty binary tree (root != Null); every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000; all node values are distinct; the number of nodes is between 1 and 1000; and there is a node in root whose value equals k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 1 <= r <= 1000.
preconditions: root is a finite nonempty binary tree (root != Null); every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000; all node values are distinct; the number of nodes is between 1 and 1000; and there is a node in root whose value equals k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if the node with value k has at least one child (that is, k is not a leaf), then r != k and d(k,r) >= 1, where d(a,b) is the number of edges on the unique simple path between the unique nodes with values a and b.
preconditions: root is a finite nonempty binary tree (root != Null); every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000; all node values are distinct; the number of nodes is between 1 and 1000; and there is a node in root whose value equals k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, d(k,r) = 0 if and only if the node with value k is a leaf of root and r = k, where d(a,b) is the number of edges on the unique simple path between the unique nodes with values a and b.
preconditions: root is a finite nonempty binary tree (root != Null); every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000; all node values are distinct; the number of nodes is between 1 and 1000; and there is a node in root whose value equals k.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, if there is exactly one value l such that Node(l, Null, Null) occurs in root, then r = l.
preconditions: root is a finite nonempty binary tree (root != Null); every node value is an integer v with 1 <= v <= 1000; all node values are distinct; the number of nodes is between 1 and 1000; and there is a node in root whose value equals k.
